newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FORECAST-Russia sees 1997 GDP growth 0-2 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Russia sees 1997 GDP growth 0-2 pct.

text.p: Growth in Russia's 1997 gross domestic product will be between zero and two percent over 1996 levels, Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin said on Wednesday.

In money terms GDP will total 2,710 trillion or 2,727 trillion roubles next year, Yasin told a conciliation commission of goverment officials and representatives of both houses of parliament reviewing the government's new 1997 budget draft.
An earlier draft forecast GDP would fall or rise by one percent fall to about 2,700 trillion roubles.
Annual inflation in 1997 will amount to between 11.5 and 11.8 percent, he said.
The government this week provided the State Duma lower house with a new draft 1997 budget after it had rejected the earlier version for unrealistic revenue and expenditure forecasts.
"So far we have no reason to make a more radical revision of the forecasts," Yasin said.
On Thursday the commission will discuss revenues and tax changes. On Friday it will discuss the deficit and the expenditure.
The new draft budget cut planned revenues to 432.8 trillion roubles from 433.64 trillion in the first draft and trimmed expenditures to 523.5 trillion roubles from 524.34 trillion.
The budget deficit remains unchanged at 3.3 percent of gross domestic product, or 90.70 trillion roubles.
Finance Minister Alexander Livshits told the commission that October tax revenues have risen by over three trillion roubles from September levels.
Tax shortfall is the most serious economic problem in Russia.

The International Monetary Fund, worried by poor tax revenues, delayed payment of next tranche of its $10 billion loan to Russia. An IMF mission will arrive in Moscow in November to examine Russia's economic performance again.
Livshits said positive changes in tax revenues had taken place between October 10 and 15.
"In November we plan to strengthen the trend," he said.
